residual_add_status.blocker: Candle Tensor::add and Tensor::broadcast_add return owned Result<Tensor> outputs and expose no caller-provided output-storage parameter.
residual_add_status.may_resume_when: An add_out/broadcast_add_out-style API or verified backend-local equivalent exists and paired Qwen3/Qwen2.5 strict CPU before/after receipts prove unchanged behavior.

candidate_frontiers.reason: Still the largest measured frontier, but current safe runtime work would run into the SLM-CPU-170 Candle residual-add output-storage blocker.
This remains model-math owned-output territory and should not be used as a bypass around the residual-add blocker without a narrower subcomponent receipt.

The tokenizer frontier is large on both Qwen3 and Qwen2.5, independent of Candle residual-add output-storage, and aligned with the Kaby lane objective to keep tokenizer/session work out of the hot loop.
This is measurable and repo-local, but it is much smaller than prompt_tokenize and should not displace the next performance frontier.

selected_frontier.scope: warm-session prompt rendering/tokenization path for strict GGUF-tokenizer Qwen3/Qwen2.5 CPU receipts
selected_frontier.why_now: It is the largest measured frontier that is not blocked by Candle residual-add caller-output-storage support.
selected_frontier.next_required_slice: Define the prompt_tokenize allocation frontier contract: identify which allocations are tokenizer-internal and which can be avoided by prompt/rendered-template/token-ID reuse, then require paired Qwen3/Qwen2.5 strict before/after receipts before any allocation or timing claim.
selected_frontier.first_allowed_runtime_change: Only after the contract exists: reuse already-rendered prompt text and token-ID vectors across repeated warm-session prompts where prompt identity matches exactly, without changing strict tokenizer provenance or prompt IDs.
